# Finance Policy — Draft

**Organization:** [Church name]  
**Effective date:** [Date]  
**Approved by:** [Board/elders/governing body]  
**Review date:** [Date]

*This is a starting template, not legal or tax advice. Fill in the approval limits and roles, then have your governing body and a qualified local accountant or attorney review it before adoption.*

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets expectations for receiving, safeguarding, spending, recording, and reporting the church’s funds. It applies to staff, leaders, volunteers, and anyone handling church money or financial records.

Church funds must be used for approved church purposes and handled transparently, consistently, and with appropriate oversight.

## 2. Financial oversight and separation of duties

The **[Finance Committee/Treasurer]** oversees financial procedures and reports to **[governing body]**. The governing body approves the annual budget, significant unbudgeted commitments, and changes to this policy.

Where practical, different people should handle authorization, payment, and reconciliation. No one should approve their own expense or be the sole person responsible for receiving, recording, and reconciling the same funds.

If staffing makes full separation impractical, the Treasurer or another designated reviewer will perform and document additional review.

## 3. Budget and financial reporting

- The Treasurer prepares an annual budget with input from ministry leaders.
- The governing body approves the budget before the start of each fiscal year.
- Ministry spending must remain within approved budget lines and this policy’s approval limits.
- The Treasurer provides the governing body with a financial report at least **[monthly/quarterly]**, including budget-versus-actual results, cash balances, and any material concerns.
- Significant variances, unexpected shortfalls, or financial risks should be raised promptly with the governing body.

## 4. Spending and purchasing

All spending must have a clear church purpose, appropriate documentation, and the required approval **before** a commitment is made.

| Amount or type | Required approval |
|---|---|
| Up to **$[A]**, within an approved budget | **[Role]** |
| **$[A]–$[B]**, within an approved budget | **[Two authorized approvers / Treasurer and ministry lead]** |
| Over **$[B]**, or any unbudgeted expense over **$[C]** | **[Governing body / designated committee]** |
| Any contract, recurring commitment, borrowing, or related-party transaction | **[Governing body]** |

- Purchases may not be divided to avoid an approval limit.
- The person requesting a purchase should not be its sole approver.
- The approver must confirm the purpose, budget availability, and supporting documentation.
- Contracts and recurring commitments must be reviewed for total cost and duration before approval.

## 5. Reimbursements and payment cards

- Reimbursement requests must be submitted within **[30] days**, with itemized receipts, the business purpose, and the budget category.
- Requests are approved by **[designated approver]**; the requester may not approve their own reimbursement.
- Reimbursements should be paid promptly after approval and recorded in the accounting system.
- Church cards may be issued only with governing-body or delegated approval. Cardholders must use them only for authorized church expenses, retain receipts, and submit reconciliations by **[monthly deadline]**.
- Personal expenses, cash advances, and card sharing are not permitted unless specifically authorized under a written procedure.

## 6. Receiving and depositing funds

- At least two people should be present when offerings or other cash are counted, where practicable.
- Counters record the total received and sign or otherwise document the count. The record should be stored securely.
- Funds should be deposited promptly, preferably within **[number] business days**. Cash must not be used directly to pay expenses.
- Donations should be recorded accurately and deposited intact. Donor restrictions must be tracked and honored.
- Donor information and giving records are confidential and accessible only to people who need them for their assigned duties.
- Gift acknowledgments and tax receipts must follow applicable local requirements. The church will not promise that a contribution is tax-deductible without confirming its eligibility.

## 7. Bank accounts and payments

- All bank and payment-processor accounts must be in the church’s legal name and approved by the governing body.
- The governing body designates authorized signers and online banking users. Access should be reviewed at least annually and removed promptly when no longer needed.
- Payments should be made by traceable methods where possible. **[Two approvals]** are required for payments above **$[limit]**.
- Blank checks must not be signed. Bank statements and payment-processor activity must be reviewed and reconciled at least monthly by someone who does not solely control the account.
- Bank reconciliations and supporting records are reviewed by **[Treasurer/another designated reviewer]** and retained.

## 8. Payroll and compensation

Compensation, benefits, reimbursements, and any changes to them must be approved by **[governing body or designated committee]**, with the affected person excluded from the decision and approval. Payroll and required reporting must be handled in accordance with applicable law and reviewed by a qualified provider where appropriate.

## 9. Conflicts of interest and related-party transactions

Anyone with a personal or financial interest in a proposed transaction must disclose it before discussion or approval. The interested person must not make the decision or approve payment. The disclosure, review, and decision must be documented. Transactions with related parties should be supported by evidence that the terms are reasonable and in the church’s interest.

## 10. Records, access, and retention

The church will maintain accurate records of income, expenses, bank activity, budgets, approvals, payroll, and restricted funds. Financial records must be stored securely, with access limited to authorized people.

Records will be retained and disposed of according to a written retention schedule that complies with applicable law and any audit, insurance, or grant requirements.

## 11. Irregularities and suspected misuse

Anyone who suspects theft, fraud, an improper payment, or a significant accounting error should promptly report it to **[Treasurer/board chair/independent contact]**. # Church Finance Policy — Draft

**Effective date:** [Date]  
**Approved by:** [Board/elders/authorized governing body]  
**Policy owner:** [Treasurer/Finance Committee]  
**Review date:** [Date]

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy establishes consistent safeguards for receiving, spending, recording, and reporting the church’s funds. It applies to staff, officers, ministry leaders, volunteers, and anyone authorized to handle church money or financial records.

This draft should be reviewed against the church’s governing documents, applicable laws, grant or donor restrictions, and advice from the church’s accountant or legal adviser before approval.

## 2. Roles and separation of duties

- The **governing body** approves the annual budget, significant unbudgeted spending, financial policies, and any exceptions to this policy.
- The **treasurer or finance lead** oversees bookkeeping, reconciliations, financial reporting, and compliance with approved controls.
- **Spending approvers** authorize expenses within the limits assigned to them.
- **Recordkeepers** enter transactions and retain supporting documentation.
- Where practical, no one person should control a transaction from beginning to end. If staffing makes separation difficult, an independent reviewer should check the transaction and its documentation.

The church will maintain a current list of people authorized to approve payments, use financial accounts, or access financial records.

## 3. Budget and spending authority

- The governing body will approve an annual budget before the start of each fiscal year.
- Ministry and staff spending must follow the approved budget and any applicable donor restrictions.
- Spending limits and approval levels will be set in an accompanying **Approval Schedule**. No person may approve their own reimbursement or a payment to themselves.
- Spending outside the approved budget, or above an assigned limit, requires approval from [designated role/body] before the commitment is made.
- The governing body must approve contracts, loans, leases, and other significant financial commitments according to the limits in the Approval Schedule.
- Budget changes and exceptions must be documented, including who approved them and when.

## 4. Donations and other receipts

- All receipts will be recorded promptly, accurately, and in the appropriate account or fund.
- Cash and checks should be counted by two people when practical. Both counters should confirm the amount in a written or electronic record.
- Funds should be deposited promptly and intact. Church receipts should not be used to pay expenses directly.
- Donation records will distinguish restricted gifts from unrestricted gifts. Restricted funds may be used only for their designated purpose, subject to applicable law and church procedures.
- Donor acknowledgments and contribution records will be handled consistently and confidentially.
- No one may promise a donor a particular use of a gift or issue a tax-related statement except under approved church procedures.

## 5. Payments, purchasing, and reimbursements

- Payments must have a legitimate church purpose, be within approved authority, and be supported by an invoice, receipt, contract, or other appropriate documentation.
- The person requesting or benefiting from a payment may not be its sole approver.
- Reimbursements must be submitted within [number] days, include itemized receipts, state the church purpose, and be approved by someone other than the claimant.
- Personal expenses may not be charged to church accounts or cards.
- Church payment cards and accounts may be used only for authorized church expenses. Cardholders must submit documentation and reconcile transactions by [deadline].
- Blank checks, shared credentials, and undocumented cash advances are not permitted.
- Any advance must be approved, recorded, and reconciled with receipts or repayment within [number] days.

## 6. Bank accounts and reconciliations

- Church accounts must be held in the church’s legal name at financial institutions approved by the governing body.
- Account signers and online access permissions will be reviewed at least [annually / upon a role change].
- Bank and payment-platform statements will be reconciled at least monthly by someone who does not have sole authority over the related transactions, where practical.
- Reconciliation differences or suspicious transactions must be investigated and reported promptly to [treasurer/finance committee/chair].
- Electronic transfers, check signing, and changes to payment instructions must follow the Approval Schedule and any additional verification procedures adopted by the church.

## 7. Financial records and reporting

- The church will maintain complete, accurate, and timely records of receipts, expenses, assets, liabilities, and restricted funds.
- Supporting documents will be retained for at least [retention period], or longer if required by law, a grant, or another obligation.
- The treasurer or finance lead will provide financial reports to [governing body/finance committee] at least [monthly/quarterly], including budget-to-actual results, cash balances, and restricted-fund balances as appropriate.
- Access to financial records will be limited to authorized people and handled confidentially.
- Any review, audit, or other independent examination required by the governing body, funders, or law will be arranged and documented.

## 8. Conflicts of interest and related-party transactions

Anyone with a personal, family, or financial interest in a proposed transaction must disclose it before discussion or approval. The interested person must not approve the transaction and should not participate in the decision except to provide requested factual information. The disclosure, decision, and basis for approval or rejection will be recorded.

## 9. Suspected errors, misuse, or fraud

Anyone who suspects a financial error, misuse of funds, fraud, or violation of this policy should report it promptly to [designated reporting contact]. If the concern involves that person, the report should go to [alternate contact]. Reports will be handled discreetly and reviewed promptly. Retaliation against someone who raises a concern in good faith is not permitted.

## 10. Policy administration

The governing body will review this policy at least annually and approve any changes. Exceptions must be documented and approved by [authorized body], except where immediate action is necessary to protect church funds; any such action must be reported and reviewed promptly.

---

## Approval Schedule — complete before adoption

| Transaction or decision | Required approval |
|---|---|
| Budgeted expense up to [amount] | [Role] |
| Budgeted expense from [amount] to [amount] | [Roles / number of approvers] |
| Expense above [amount] | [Governing body / designated committee] |
| Unbudgeted expense up to [amount] | [Role] |
| Contract, lease, or loan | [Approving body and threshold] |
| Reimbursement to an officer or staff member | [Independent approver] |
| New bank account or change of signer | [Approving body] |

This is a working draft, not a determination that it meets your local legal or tax requirements. Before adoption, fill in the approval limits, roles, deadlines, and retention period, then have the appropriate governing body and qualified adviser review it.
